rows.grounds: indeclinable indicating manner; refers to the state described in preceding verses
genitive of agent in that state; from sthita (abiding/situated)
ablative indicating source or cause; bodha as awakening/knowing
demonstrative referring to the previously indicated reality
essential form or nature; object of partaking
one who shares or partakes in; from bhaj

items.question: By what means does one abiding thus come to partake of that own nature?
premises: One is abiding in the state described previously.
Meditation is presented as a means to realization.
Awareness is presented as an alternative means to realization.
items.inference: Therefore, one abiding thus partakes of that own nature either through meditation or through awareness.
uncertainties: Whether bodhāt indicates spontaneous awareness or a specific cognitive event is not fully explicit.
items.plain_english: For one who abides thus, through meditation or through awareness, there is partaking of that own nature.
